from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Cones are surfaces formed by rotation.", "Slicing cones creates conic sections.", "Circles, ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas emerge."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Slicing Problem", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        label_cone = Text("Cone", font_size=24, color=WHITE)

        intersection = Circle(radius=0.7, color=PURPLE, stroke_width=4)
        label_inter = Text("Intersection", font_size=24, color=PURPLE)

        # Positioning
        self.place_in_area(cone, "A2", "C5", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(label_cone, "A2")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(cone), Write(label_cone))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        self.place_in_area(intersection, "C3", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(intersection), Write(label_inter), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PURPLE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(cone.animate.rotate(PI/6, axis=OUT), intersection.animate.rotate(PI/6, axis=OUT), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Universal Application", ["This holds for all conics.", "Parabolas use one sphere tangency.", "Hyperbolas use two spheres tangency."])
        
        # Parabola Visualization (Placeholder geometries for representation)
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2).rotate(PI/4, axis=RIGHT)
        sphere1 = Sphere(radius=0.4).set_color(BLUE)
        parabola_curve = ParametricFunction(lambda t: np.array([t, 0.5*t**2, 0]), t_range=[-1, 1])
        
        parabola_group = VGroup(cone, sphere1, parabola_curve).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(parabola_group, 'B2')
        
        # Hyperbola Visualization
        cone2 = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2).rotate(PI/4, axis=RIGHT)
        sphere2 = Sphere(radius=0.3).set_color(RED)
        sphere3 = Sphere(radius=0.3).set_color(RED).shift(DOWN*0.5)
        hyperbola_curve = ParametricFunction(lambda t: np.array([t, np.sqrt(1+t**2), 0]), t_range=[-1, 1])
        
        hyperbola_group = VGroup(cone2, sphere2, sphere3, hyperbola_curve).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(hyperbola_group, 'E2')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(parabola_group), Create(hyperbola_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(sphere1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(sphere2), Indicate(sphere3))
        
        # Final Highlight
        self.play(parabola_group.animate.set_color("#00CCFF"), hyperbola_group.animate.set_color("#00CCFF"))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", ["Conics are 3D geometric results.", "Spheres link visuals to algebra.", "Dandelin spheres unify conic properties."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show all three conic types appearing from slices. Color: #FFFFFF.
        c1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        c2 = Ellipse(width=1.0, height=0.6, color=WHITE).set_fill(RED, opacity=0.3)
        c3 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, x_range=[-1, 1], color=WHITE).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.3).scale(0.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(c1, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(c2, 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(c3, 'B6')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(c1), FadeIn(c2), FadeIn(c3))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the common Dandelin sphere principle. Color: #FFFF00.
        sphere1 = Sphere(radius=0.3, color=YELLOW).set_opacity(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere1, 'D3')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere1))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade all elements into a unified diagram. Color: #FFFFFF.
        group = VGroup(c1, c2, c3, sphere1)
        self.play(group.animate.move_to(self.grid['E4']), FadeOut(c1), FadeOut(c2), FadeOut(c3))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Unlocking the Geometry of Cones: Dandelin Spheres
outline.target_audience: High school geometry students or early undergraduate math enthusiasts

sections.title: Introduction: The Slicing Problem
sections.content: Define the cone and the plane intersection. Briefly review prerequisite knowledge: A cone is a surface formed by rotating a line around an axis. When we slice it, we get conic sections (circles, ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas).
sections.example: Imagine slicing a carrot with a knife at different angles to create different cross-sections.

sections.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
sections.content: Visual setup: Introduce two imaginary spheres inscribed inside the cone, tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the slicing plane (at a point). This is the 'Aha!' moment where 3D geometry explains 2D shapes.
sections.example: Visualize two floating bubbles inside a party hat, touching the 'slice' paper at specific points (foci).

sections.title: The Ellipse Connection
sections.content: Show how the distances from any point on the intersection ellipse to the two contact points of the spheres sum up to a constant (the distance between the two circles of tangency). This bridges the gap between 'slicing' and the algebraic definition of an ellipse.
sections.example: A 'pinball' animation where a ball bounces between the two sphere contact points, maintaining a constant path length.

sections.title: Universal Application
sections.content: Briefly demonstrate that this principle holds for parabolas and hyperbolas (using one or two spheres). Explain why this is important: it proves that the geometric 'foci' of conics are not just abstract points, but physical contact points of spheres.
sections.example: A satellite dish (parabolic) receiving signals that all converge to the 'sphere contact point' (the focus).

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Conic sections aren't just equations; they are the natural result of 3D geometry. Dandelin spheres unify the visual 'slice' with the algebraic 'focus-directrix' properties.
sections.example: An animation morphing a circular slice into an elliptical one, showing the spheres growing and shifting to accommodate the change.
